subject: Follow-up: Throughput profile & $/1M token target (FinPlatform POC)
messages:
From: Jay Patel <jay.patel@finplatform.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T20:12:00Z
Subject: Intro / Throughput profile (FinPlatform POC)

Thanks for the demo today — good conversation, appreciate the clarity on routing and fallbacks. High-level numbers from our side so you can start an econ sketch: 

- Monthly token volume (est): baseline ~200M tokens/month; campaign bursts up to ~1.2B tokens in a strong month.
- Request shape: majority short interactions for our chat assistant (avg input ~80 tokens, avg output ~260 tokens → ~340 tokens/resp). A smaller set of longer retrieval + summarize flows (~2% of calls, ~1.5–2k tokens each).
- Traffic pattern: steady daytime usage (US hours), sustained baseline ~30–50 RPS, peak spiky bursts up to ~160 RPS during product announcements.~80% of calls are latency-sensitive (sub-500ms target at the p95), 20% can be async/batched.
- Concurrency expectation: application-level concurrency target is ~120 concurrent active requests at peak; we expect to front a few endpoints (chat / search / summarize) with different latency profiles.
- Target unit economics: procurement asked us to aim for a ballpark $/1M tokens that makes this viable for our model — they'd like something in the ~$350–$600 per 1M tokens range depending on SLA & commitment.

Next steps from our side: procurement will want a committed option + a hosted option. Can you provide two pricing scenarios (hosted pay-as-you-go and 12-mo committed with reduced $/1M)? Also if you can call out assumptions about continuous batching effects and expected effective tokens-per-second savings that would be helpful.

Thanks — looping in procurement shortly.

--
Jay Patel
Head of Platform, FinPlatform
jay.patel@finplatform.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jay Patel <jay.patel@finplatform.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T01:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro / Throughput profile (FinPlatform POC)

Jay — thanks, this is super helpful. Summary & immediate asks from Redwood: 

Summary of your inputs (to confirm):
- Baseline ~200M tokens/mo, bursts to ~1.2B/mo (campaign-driven).
- Avg request ~340 tokens, 80% latency-sensitive, 20% batchable/async.
- Peak concurrent active requests ~120; sustained baseline 30–50 RPS.
- Target $/1M tokens: ~$350–$600 depending on SLA/commitment.

What we'll provide next (deliverables):
1) Two pricing scenarios: hosted (pay-as-you-go) and 12-month committed capacity with a committed throughput/discount ladder. Each will show an effective $/1M tokens and the assumptions for batching, caching, and prefix reuse.
2) A short econ estimate (PDF) showing token-level math, estimated savings from continuous batching, and a sensitivity table for different concurrency profiles.
3) Suggested configuration for the POC: single model shard with autoscale to cover baseline → target peak, plus reserved pre-warm for the first 60s of announced campaigns.

Quick clarifying Qs to make the econ accurate: 
- Of the 20% batchable traffic, how often will you schedule batch windows vs. ad-hoc background jobs? (If you can share % of batch in fixed windows that materially improves batching efficiency.)
- Any hard latency SLOs per endpoint (p50/p95/p99)? You mentioned p95 < 500ms for the chat flow — is that a hard requirement for the POC or a stretch goal?

Cc'ing Ben (solutions) to include continuous-batch assumptions and to attach an initial econ file. Priyom, I may loop you on the pricing ladder once Ben and I align on the batch savings assumptions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jay Patel <jay.patel@finplatform.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T04:30:00Z
Subject: RE: Intro / Throughput profile (FinPlatform POC)

Great context — added a few technical assumptions so the econ is grounded: 

Technical assumptions we plan to use in the econ model:
- Continuous batching: for short-turn chat requests (avg ~340 tokens) we assume continuous batching will deliver a 22–38% compute reduction versus naive single-request execution for the given shape (depends on peak alignment). We model a median 30% improvement in token-efficiency for the hosted case and 35% for dedicated/reserved (better packing because of pinned capacity).
- Prefix/KV cache reuse: we measured ~15–20% prefix reuse for similar customers — we'll conservatively model 12% effective token savings from KV reuse on chat flows.
- Effective token amplification: longer retrieval flows (2% of calls) amplify tokens by ~4–6x; we model them separately to avoid skewing the short-request econ.
- Concurrency budgeting: to keep p95 < 500ms with continuous batching, we recommend configuring initial concurrency headroom of ~1.25x of observed peak (so plan for ~150 active slots when you expect 120 peak). Autoscale rules should target 60–80ms queueing thresholds per slot.

Attachments: I attached a first-pass econ estimate (redwood-econ-estimate-v2.pdf) and a POC activity map (FP-POC-MAP.xlsx) with a proposed timeline and test cases. The econ sheet includes a sensitivity table for $/1M tokens with and without batching and with varying commitment levels.

If you can confirm: the percent of batchable traffic and whether you can run a 2-week campaign simulation during the POC (to capture burst packing effects), we can tighten the estimate.

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Jay Patel <jay.patel@finplatform.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, FinPlatform Procurement <procurement@finplatform.com>

Subject: Re: Intro / Throughput profile (FinPlatform POC)

Thanks team — this is exactly what procurement needs. Quick answers: 
- Batchable traffic: roughly two thirds of the 20% (so ~13% total) we can schedule into nightly batch windows; the other ~7% is ad-hoc async. We'll commit to a 2-week campaign simulation during the POC (we can coordinate exact dates).
- Latency SLO: chat p95 target 450ms for the POC (hard requirement); p99 we can tolerate up to 900ms as a stretch. Search/summarize endpoints are fine to be async up to a few seconds.
- Procurement contact: Megha Iyer <megha.iyer@finplatform.com> — she'll evaluate the 12-mo committed option and needs the SOW + pricing ladder.

Next steps: 
1) Redwood to send two pricing scenarios + the econ PDF by EOD Thursday (your timezone).
2) We'll schedule a 30-min follow-up Thurs or Fri to review assumptions and lock the POC simulation window.
3) Procurement (Megha) will be on the next thread to review SOW/place an initial PO if the committed scenario meets their constraints.

Thanks — looking forward.

--
Jay Patel
Head of Platform, FinPlatform
